summary: No orders today: the account stays entirely in cash because bitcoin fell to about $55,000, its lowest since September 2024, before bouncing back to about $60,000, and it is still far below all of its averages, so none of my conditions for buying back has been met.
thesis:
Where the account stands. The account is $988.30 in cash and holds no coins, about 1.2% below its $1,000 start. A plain $1,000 bitcoin holding bought on 11 November was worth $795.58 at the end of 20 November, so the account is about $193 ahead of simply holding bitcoin. All of that lead comes from having been out of the market since 14 November.

What happened. Bitcoin's last price of 20 November on Coinbase was $58,815, down 5.0% on the day. Early on Saturday 21 November the selling went further: reported lows range from below $57,000 to about $55,250, the lowest since September 2024. Then it rebounded sharply, to about $60,190 at 15:16 UTC and about $60,280 in a later snapshot, nearly 9% off the low. About $2.4 billion of borrowed bets across crypto were forcibly closed over 24 hours, over $1 billion of them in bitcoin. Ether recovered to about $1,690, solana to about $71 and XRP to about $0.93 in the same snapshot, after XRP had dipped near $0.87 overnight. One fund was reported by an on-chain tracker to have bought about 10,000 bitcoin near $58,650 during the fall. The pages I read gave no clear cause for the latest leg down beyond the continuing sell-off in technology shares and the forced selling it set off.

The trend. Using the figures collected for this account (last price of 20 November), and with bitcoin now near $60,000, it is about 15% below its 20-day average ($71,010), about 23% below its 50-day average ($77,625) and about 17% below its 200-day average ($72,530). It has fallen 24% over 20 days and 32% over 60. Every other watched coin is also below all three of its averages and down 24% to 28% over 20 days. Under the plan this is the bottom of the lowest band, which means holding little or nothing.

The case for buying, taken seriously. A flush to a new low followed by a quick 9% bounce, with billions in borrowed bets wiped out and a large buyer stepping in, is the kind of pattern that sometimes marks the end of a fall. But one weekend bounce from a new low is not a turn in the trend: bitcoin is still below its level of a day ago before the drop began, below the $62,000 floor that held from 14 to 19 November, and I found no sign that money has started flowing back into the US bitcoin funds. Weekend trading is also thinner, so moves can reverse quickly. Buying now would be betting on a bottom, which the plan does not do.

What would bring me back, unchanged. I will buy bitcoin again if it ends a UTC day back above its 200-day average, now about $72,500, or earlier with a smaller amount (about 15% to 20% of the account) if it holds above $70,000 for two UTC days while the bitcoin funds take in money on most days. A lasting return above $62,000 together with fund inflows would be an early sign the fall is ending, though not enough alone to buy. Given how far the price is from these levels, I will look at the next run at whether a lower first step is justified if the bounce holds and fund flows turn positive, rather than change the rule on a single day's move. This view is wrong if today's low proves to be the bottom and bitcoin climbs steadily from here, in which case the account would buy back at a higher price and give back part of its lead.
risks: The main risk is missing a sharp rebound: today's low came with very large forced selling and an immediate 9% bounce, which is how some falls end, and my buy-back levels sit about 15% to 20% above the price, so a recovery could go a long way before the account takes part. Prices here come from news reports published at different times, and the two reports I read disagree on the exact low ($55,250 versus below $57,000); the latest reliable reading is from mid-afternoon UTC on a Saturday, and bitcoin can move several percent before midnight UTC. I found no reliable 2026 figures for US bitcoin fund flows on 20 November.
